item.title: Chancay Port boosts South America-Asia links 2 years on
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
This photo taken on Nov. 3, 2026 shows a view of the Chancay Port in Chancay, Peru. Two years after its inauguration on Peru's Pacific coast, Chancay Port is handling growing cargo volumes, expanding shipping connections with Asia and creating new employment opportunities for local residents.(Photo by Mariana Bazo/Xinhua) LIMA, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Two years after its inauguration on Peru's Pacific coast, Chancay Port is handling growing cargo volumes, expanding shipping connections with Asia and creating new employment opportunities for local residents. The Chinese-built port, inaugurated in November 2024, has emerged as an increasingly important gateway for South American exports to Asia. Its expanding network of shipping routes is helping businesses access overseas markets while generating economic opportunities for the nearby town of Chancay. The second anniversary of the port's debut came just days before China's hosting of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings. The Shenzhen gathering's theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," is reflected in the growing importance of trans-Pacific trade and transport connectivity, as exemplified by Chancay Port. As it continues to expand, the logistics hub is strengthening links between South America and Asia, providing fresh momentum for trans-Pacific trade and deeper regional economic cooperation. SMARTER, MORE EFFICIENT OPERATIONS As South America's first smart port, Chancay is equipped with six remote-controlled ship-to-shore cranes, 15 automated rail-mounted gantry cranes and 50 intelligent container trucks. By integrating artificial intelligence, digital twin technology and the Internet of Things, the port has adopted a technology-driven operating model that enables round-the-clock operations, with cargo handling processes increasingly automated and digitally monitored. In the first nine months of this year, Chancay Port handled 323 vessel calls, up 31 percent year on year, while container throughput rose 47 percent, to 340,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs). Over the past two years, the port has continued to expand its shipping network, diversify its business portfolio and improve its operational efficiency. Through the two-way Chancay-Shanghai express shipping service and regional feeder routes connecting major ports along South America's west coast and in Central America, the port has developed an initial network combining direct transoceanic shipping with regional cargo distribution, extending its reach to neighboring countries like Colombia, Ecuador and Chile. Ecuador's Association of Banana Marketing and Export (ACORBANEC) Executive Director Richard Salazar said the shipping route linking Ecuador's Guayaquil Port with Chancay Port has cut the time at sea for Ecuadorian bananas to reach China to about 27 days, creating more favorable conditions for local exporters to tap the Chinese market. Figures released in September by ACORBANEC showed that the country exported 12.14 million boxes of bananas to China in the first eight months of 2026, up about 11.84 percent year on year. PORT DEVELOPMENT BRINGS LOCAL BENEFITS Located about 80 km north of Peru's capital Lima, Chancay Port has brought tangible changes to local communities since it began regular operations, generating new jobs and business opportunities. The port's development has opened up new employment prospects for young people in the area. Monica Bisso, 28, is among those who have benefited. Born and raised in Chancay, she had long hoped to find work in her hometown. "When I saw the port's recruitment announcement, I submitted my application without hesitation," she said. Today, Bisso works as an operator of automated rail-mounted gantry cranes at the port. Bisso told Xinhua that after joining the company, she received a month of theoretical instruction and hands-on training, equipping her with the skills needed for the job. "I've had the opportunity to learn more about different fields, and with my higher income, I can now start building a new house," she said, adding that the port's continued development has also helped nearby residents acquire new skills and improve their livelihoods. Growth in port operations has attracted more businesses along the supply chain to establish a presence in and around Chancay. An increasing number of visitors and companies seeking business opportunities have also helped boost local commerce and services. Itala Ramirez, a 55-year-old local resident, told Xinhua that before the port was built, she had to leave her hometown to take on physically demanding jobs elsewhere. "I now work for a port cargo handling company and have a stable income close to home. I'm very happy with that," Ramirez said, beaming. CONNECTING ASIA-PACIFIC FOR A SHARED FUTURE According to a report released on Nov. 6 by the Peruvian Exporters Association, Peru's exports to China reached 31.309 billion U.S. dollars in the first nine months of 2026, up 31.3 percent year on year and accounting for 37.4 percent of the country's total exports. China is Peru's largest export destination, and trade through Chancay Port has injected fresh momentum into economic and trade cooperation between China and Peru and the broader Latin America region. Danper Trujillo, a Peruvian agricultural exporter, ships fresh blueberries, avocados and table grapes to China and other Asian countries mainly through Chancay Port. Brigitte Grados, deputy manager of international operations in the company's supply chain department, told Xinhua that Chancay enjoys a strategic geographical advantage as a departure port for Asian markets and offers highly competitive shipping times. "Cargo shipped from Chancay to Shanghai can also be connected through Shanghai Port to other Asian ports, such as Busan in South Korea," she said. Technology products, fast-moving consumer goods and other shipments arriving at Chancay are subsequently transported by air or land to countries including Bolivia, Colombia and Brazil. Jhon Valdiglesias, a researcher at the Center for Asian Studies of Peru's National University of San Marcos, said the construction and operation of infrastructure projects such as Chancay Port are facilitating deeper Asia-Pacific cooperation. As connectivity improves and trade and investment ties grow closer, regional economies are expected to develop a mutually reinforcing cycle of growth and cooperation, he said. Juan Carlos Paz, former head of Peru's National Port Authority, also told Xinhua that "Chancay Port has become a trans-Pacific shipping hub." The port's continued development is providing new momentum for trans-Pacific trade and deeper regional economic cooperation, he said. ■ Workers unload materials at the Chancay Port in Chancay, Peru, Nov. 3, 2026. Two years after its inauguration on Peru's Pacific coast, Chancay Port is handling growing cargo volumes, expanding shipping connections with Asia and creating new employment opportunities for local residents.(Photo by Mariana Bazo/Xinhua) Staff members monitor operations from an office at the Chancay Port in Chancay, Peru, Nov. 3, 2026. item.title: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Wednesday that China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. He said that China-Russia ties set an example for a new model of major-country relations featuring equality, mutual respect, good faith, and win-win cooperation. Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations. Both sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to ensure that the consensus reached by the two heads of state is effectively implemented, Xi said. Xi called on the two countries to provide a more stable and predictable investment and business environment and protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises from both countries. The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation, Xi noted. China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said. Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said. Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said. Russia also stands ready to work with China to promote development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, advance the process toward a multipolar world and build a more just and equitable global governance system, he added. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu)

item.title: Xi welcomes Trump at Shenzhen airport
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. Trump is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday welcomed U.S. President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in south China's Guangdong Province. Trump is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Amid welcome music, Xi and Trump shook hands warmly. Honor guards of the Chinese People's Liberation Army presented arms to salute, and a girl handed the U.S. leader a bouquet. The national flags of China and the United States fluttered in the wind as a military band played the national anthems of the two countries, and fighter jets flew overhead in salute. The two heads of state waved to a welcoming young crowd. Xi recalled his state visit to the United States in September this year, when the U.S. presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcome ceremony, noting that China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill. Extending his welcome to Trump for visiting China again, Xi said that he looks forward to conducting in-depth exchanges with the U.S. president on major issues concerning bilateral relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape to advance a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. Trump thanked Xi for greeting him in person at the airport and for the special arrangements by the Chinese side. He said it is a great pleasure to visit China again, calling China a great country and Xi a great leader. Trump said that every meeting with Xi had been very pleasant, and he believes that the visit will further advance bilateral relations and achieve complete success. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. item.title: APEC CEO Summit 2026 releases Shenzhen initiative, calling for shared prosperity in Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhen initiative of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 was released on Wednesday, calling for deepening an open regional economy, driving inclusive growth through technological innovation, strengthening regional connectivity, and working together to achieve shared prosperity. This marks the first time in the 30-year history of the summit that an outcome document has been issued in the form of an initiative. The initiative states that, guided by four priority areas -- openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven growth, greater connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation -- the Asia-Pacific business community stands ready to work with all economies to fully implement the Putrajaya Vision 2040 and build an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community. It also calls for translating this year's APEC theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," into concrete actions, so that the Asia-Pacific region continues to serve as the world's most dynamic engine of growth and a community of shared prosperity. ■

item.title: Xi calls for advancing steady, sound development of China-ROK relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Republic of Korea (ROK) Lee Jae Myung, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called for advancing the steady and sound development of relations between China and the Republic of Korea (ROK) as next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two "friendly neighbors and strategic cooperative partners." Xi made the remarks during his meeting with ROK President Lee Jae Myung, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. The two countries should uphold strategic independence, maintain the political foundation for bilateral relations, and further consolidate and develop the relationship, Xi stressed. China and the ROK have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement. The two countries should make full use of this institutional arrangement to strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and foster a collaborative ecosystem for emerging technology industries such as artificial intelligence, Xi said. China also stands ready to work with the ROK to facilitate people-to-people exchanges and carry out sound and beneficial cultural exchanges in a step-by-step manner, Xi said. The two sides should further strengthen multilateral coordination, jointly uphold true multilateralism, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community and the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, make greater contributions to regional peace and development, and maintain the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Xi said. For his part, Lee said that the two countries have seen sustained momentum in the comprehensive restoration of ROK-China relations, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation growing rapidly, people-to-people exchanges becoming increasingly frequent, and mutual perceptions steadily improving. The ROK's commitment to the one-China policy has not changed and will not change, Lee stressed. The ROK hopes to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, and industrial and supply chains, foster closer people-to-people bonds, and pursue a more mature ROK-China strategic partnership, he said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Republic of Korea (ROK) Lee Jae Myung, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu)

item.title: Full text
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday delivered a keynote speech at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The following is the full text of the speech: Forging Ahead with Resolve Toward a Bright Future for the Asia-Pacific Keynote Speech by H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China At the APEC CEO Summit Shenzhen, November 18, 2026 Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Friends, Good morning! I wish to extend my welcome to you all, leaders of business communities of the Asia-Pacific. I am so delighted to meet you here in Shenzhen. Shenzhen, on the shores of the South China Sea, embraces the surging winds and waves of the ocean. Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development. There is so much people can draw from Shenzhen's success. Today, we find ourselves in a changing and turbulent world. Global growth lacks momentum, and unilateralism and protectionism are rampant. Still, global trade keeps growing against headwinds, and breakthroughs are being made in emerging technologies at a faster pace, exerting a profound impact on global development. What is going on with the world? What should we do in the Asia-Pacific? To open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? These are hard questions of our times that we must answer. As an ancient Chinese saying goes, all approaches should adapt to changing times to remain relevant. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of our times. This year, China is hosting APEC for the third time. We are ready to work with all other parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and bring prosperity for all in our region. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should uphold peace and stability. There can be no prosperity without security, and no security without stability. Thanks to the stable environment in our region over the past decades, the Asia-Pacific has maintained steady economic progress and become an important engine driving global growth. The more complex the external conditions become, the more important it is for us to uphold the postwar international order, and promote an equality-based and orderly multipolar world and economic globalization that is inclusive and brings benefit to all. It is even more important for us to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, and overcome challenges through solidarity and cooperation. This is the way to cement the foundation for sustaining peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should build bridges of opening up and cooperation. History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind. We should firmly safeguard the WTO-centered, rules-based multilateral trading system, support free and open trade and investment, and keep global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. We should work steadily toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, build a multidimensional connectivity network, enhance cooperation in areas such as digital transformation of trade, cross-border e-commerce, and smart customs, and deepen international cooperation on industrial and supply chains. All this will pave the way for greater economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should boost innovation to drive growth. Innovation is crucial for progress. APEC members have driven global scientific and technological innovation: Unicorn companies and large AI models have emerged in large numbers, and many innovations have empowered hundreds of trades and industries and reached millions of households. We should forge science, technology and innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and AI, and promote green and low-carbon transition. By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should expand our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. As the economies in our region differ in history, culture and stage of development, taking a uniform approach will not advance cooperation. We should remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy. At the same time, we should promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness. We should follow a people-centered development philosophy, strengthen economic and technical cooperation geared for developing economies, and deepen cooperation in transportation, public health, energy, food security, anti-corruption and other fields, so that development fruits are shared by all economies and all groups and communities. The Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects. Shenzhen, where we are now meeting, is part of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific. Distinguished Guests, Dear Friends, This year marks the start of China's 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development. China's economy maintains a strong momentum of high-quality, innovation-driven growth, demonstrating great resilience and vitality. In the first three quarters, the Chinese economy grew by 4.6 percent. New quality productive forces are developing more quickly, a new pattern of development is being fostered at a faster pace, and green and low-carbon transition is steadily picking up speed. The 15th Five-Year Plan has gotten off to a good start. A blueprint for China's development, the 15th Five-Year Plan also provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. Indeed, it is an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world. -- China will provide global business communities with a super-sized open market. China is the world's second largest consumer market. It has the largest middle income group in the world and enormous potential for investment and consumption. From new energy vehicles to smart homes, from the silver economy to ice and snow tourism, every new growth area is creating new opportunities for businesses across the world. As China accelerates the development of a big, open market and increases import of quality products and services, more diverse demands will be unleashed. Recently, the ninth China International Import Expo was held in Shanghai. Many of you present today attended the Expo and found new cooperation opportunities. China will also continue to host "Export to China" series and other events to open efficient channels to help quality products from across the world enter the Chinese market. -- China will provide global business communities with a promising land for development. Innovation-driven growth and green transition are the keywords in observing China's economy. From factory and farm robots, to autonomous driving and drone delivery, China is a super-sized innovation testing ground where frontier technologies are tested, improved and upgraded in real-world scenarios, and are then turned into high-quality growth drivers. China will step up efforts to build modernized industrial system, and deepen integration between technological and industrial innovation. It will support the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries, the expansion of emerging industries, and the forward-looking planning of industries of the future. This will generate strong impetus for technological innovation and growth of businesses around the world. -- China will provide global business communities with an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. In 2001, China hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting for the first time and joined the World Trade Organization in the same year. Over the past 25 years, China has fully honored its WTO accession commitments. While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development. China has stood up to unilateralism and protectionism, and remained committed to true multilateralism, to upholding the multilateral trading system and WTO rules, and to advancing WTO reform; it has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation. No matter how the international landscape may evolve, China will not waver in its pursuit of win-win cooperation with all other countries. China stays firmly committed to high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and welcomes the active participation of businesses from across the Asia-Pacific so that we can create growth opportunities and share the fruits of development together. China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access but also go a step further -- we will carry out reform in challenging areas, such as rules, regulation and standards, in order to fully ensure market access and an accommodating operating environment in the manufacturing sector, to steadily expand opening up in the service sector, and to foster a more stable and more predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China. Distinguished Guests, Dear Friends, The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation. Asia-Pacific business communities are pioneers of the global economy. I hope you will carry forward the entrepreneurial spirit, boldly pursue innovation and excellence, explore and expand opportunities for business cooperation, and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. You are more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization. Let us join hands to meet challenges facing development through opening up, generate momentum for growth through innovation, and pursue prosperity for all through cooperation. Let us work together to build an Asia-Pacific community and deliver a bright future for our region. Thank you. ■

item.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Tao) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all. Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day summit has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. "The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade. As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination. Xi said the Asia-Pacific should support free and open trade and investment while keeping the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. "History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. He stressed the need to forge partnerships in science, technology and innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon development. "By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," the president said. The region should also remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, and promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness, Xi said. According to Xi, there is much to draw from the success of Shenzhen, host of this year's APEC CEO Summit and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development, Xi said. Noting that the Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects, Xi said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. "This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific," he said. Looking ahead, as China's ties with the Asia-Pacific grow increasingly close, Xi said China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. The development blueprint is "an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world," he said. Xi said China will provide the global business community with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, as well as an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. He highlighted China's accelerating efforts to develop a big, open market and build a modern industrial system, pledging a more stable and predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China. Calling the Asia-Pacific business communities "pioneers of the global economy," he said they are "more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization." Leaders of APEC economies, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, attended the summit. Having previously hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings in 2001 and 2014, China is taking on the role of APEC host for the third time this year. It has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year and reached nearly 50 practical outcomes with other APEC economies in the economic and trade field. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. item.title: Xi hosts welcome banquet for guests attending APEC meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. "On behalf of the Chinese government and people, I wish to extend a warm welcome to all the distinguished guests," Xi said in his toast. Openness is deeply rooted in Shenzhen's DNA and innovation drives the city's vitality, while cooperation is where its strength comes from, Xi said, adding that the success of Shenzhen is also a microcosm of China's reform and opening up, as well as an example of fruitful cooperation across the Asia-Pacific. Noting that openness, innovation and cooperation have been the distinctive features of APEC since its establishment, Xi said APEC has grasped the pulse of the times and guided the process of regional economic integration, making the Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region and a vital growth engine of the world economy. "At the economic leaders' meeting tomorrow, we will discuss measures to expand two-way opening up, explore paths of innovation-driven growth and unfold more opportunities of practical cooperation in various fields," Xi said. ■

item.title: APEC: Striving Together for Shared Prosperity

Twelve years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping invoked the image of swan geese, calling on APEC economies to enhance cooperation and embark on a new flight. Today, across the vast Pacific, the APEC family sails together toward shared prosperity and a brighter future.
